title: Protection Premium Still to Be Collected and the Granite Ridge Credit Application
content:
Where a Pass and Trip Protection plan written over a season pass on the household account still has premium to be collected, that premium is held back from the amount drawn in a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme credit application, because the pass account will present it alongside the next instalment. The points below set out how much is held back.

*How much is held back where the collective's protection records show such a plan with premium still to be collected and that plan stands with a settled claim?* The whole of the premium still to be collected is held back.

*And where those records show such a plan with premium still to be collected standing in any other state?* Half of the premium still to be collected is held back, a share of 50 per cent of it.

*And in any other case?* Nothing is held back on this account.

*Which plan is read?* A Pass and Trip Protection record on the same household account whose covered holding is a season pass. Two things are read from it: the premium still to be collected on that plan, and the state the plan stands in.

*What of a plan with no premium still to be collected?* Nothing is held back on this account, whatever state the plan stands in; and where no such plan stands on the household account at all, nothing is held back either.

*What is the amount held back deducted from?* The rounded figure the share drawn produces, not the pot.

*Worked on a hypothetical account.* A household holding a Pass and Trip Protection plan over a Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass, with 84.00 of premium still to be collected and a claim settled on the plan: the whole 84.00 is held back. Where the same plan stood with no claim settled on it, half of 84.00 would be held back, which is 42.00.
